x.ASV: O praise Jehovah, all ye nations; Laud him, all ye peoples.
x.Darby: Praise Jehovah, all ye nations; laud him, all ye peoples;
x.KJV: O praise the Lord, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people.
x.YLT: Praise Jehovah, all ye nations, Glorify Him, all ye peoples.

nt: These two phrases **Praise Yahweh, all nations** and **extol him, all peoples** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [Praise Yahweh, all nations; yes, extol him, all peoples]

Here, **all nations** represents the people in all nations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [you people in all nations]

x.ASV: For his lovingkindness is great toward us; And the truth of Jehovah endureth for ever. Praise ye Jehovah.
x.Darby: For his loving-kindness is great toward us, and the truth of Jehovah [endureth] for ever. Hallelujah!
x.KJV: For his merciful kindness is great toward us: and the truth of the Lord endureth for ever. Praise ye the Lord.
x.YLT: For mighty to us hath been His kindness, And the truth of Jehovah is to the age. Praise ye Jah!

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [For he will never stop being faithful to his covenant to love us]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **trustworthiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh will be trustworthy to do this forever]

The words **Hallelu Yah** are Hebrew words, containing a plural command to praise Yahweh. You will need to decide if you will use these words in their Hebrew form or if you will instead translate the meaning into your language. Either approach has broad support. If you use the Hebrew words, you could spell them the way that they sound in your language and then put the translation in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Halleluia] or [Praise Yah]
**Yah** is a shortened form of the name “Yahweh,” the God of Israel. You could use the full name if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh]
